claim_scope: Research-only bounded replay evidence for the first ZenoDEX Tau ADT logical ABI. The asset-transfer module uses current Tau ADTs, whole/sub-tuple definition arguments, mixed sbf/bitvector members and min() to encode command/context/result structural rails including the exact no-op rejection contract and the NEW-6 post-state resource-bound rejection abstraction. The lane-journal module uses nested ADTs, whole/sub-tuple arguments, recurrence relations and min() to encode structural journal bindings and a saturating replay cursor. Replay builds and executes the exact pinned IDNI/tau-lang source commit, streams the long upstream build outside pytest capture, requires exactly one final Tau T/F verdict per query, and includes a deliberate over-strong ADT statement that must return F so unexpanded or stale REPL output cannot masquerade as success.
failure_modes: a rejected asset-transfer result changes the abstract state root or carries effects
POST_STATE_RESOURCE_BOUND_EXCEEDED is not represented as a closed typed no-op rejection
a whole or nested ADT call silently fails to match its flattened predicate arity
a lane journal accepts zero abstract effect-plan or receipt roots despite the Python contract
the replay cursor wraps from the maximum bv[16] value to zero
the evidence is replayed against a mutable or different Tau source revision
an earlier T in REPL output hides a final F or an unexpanded application
a silent nested upstream build is terminated before producing a semantic verdict
Tau Tables are claimed or used before first-class Tables support is available

aaa.reason: The pinned replay arranges closed quantified ADT domains and explicit boundary values, acts through Tau's own valid/unsat decision commands on the exact upstream source pin, and requires exactly one T/F verdict matching the expected result. A deliberately over-strong ADT statement must return F before any positive replay is accepted.

reject_is_noop.reason: The asset-transfer ADT contract and replay explicitly require every rejected result, including abstract reject code 12 for POST_STATE_RESOURCE_BOUND_EXCEEDED, to preserve the pre/post state-root tag and assert effects_empty = 1.

boundary_dimensions.name: asset_transfer_result_algebra
points: rejected uses closed codes 1..12, preserves the state-root tag and has effects_empty 1

boundary_dimensions.name: fee_cap_min_equivalence
points: required_fee <= cap makes min(required_fee, cap) equal required_fee
required_fee > cap makes the equality false

boundary_dimensions.name: replay_cursor_saturation
points: non-max bv[16] values advance by exactly one
the all-ones maximum remains fixed and never wraps

boundary_dimensions.name: adt_flattening
points: whole command/result/journal values match one parameter per flattened member
nested context/header/binding sub-tuples flatten correctly when followed by scalar arguments

boundary_dimensions.name: harness_verdict
points: a deliberately false whole-ADT implication produces exactly one F verdict
every admitted positive or negative replay query produces exactly one expected T verdict

nonclaims: This evidence grants no production, settlement, publication, verifier, migration, release, or value-moving authority.
bv[8]/bv[16] roots, identifiers and amounts are bounded abstract tags; this is not a 128-bit or 256-bit production arithmetic model.
This evidence does not validate hashing, signatures, canonical serialization, receipt proofs, table storage, table roots, or Tau Net consensus integration.
This evidence does not claim first-class Tau Tables support; no executable Table construct appears in the two Tau specifications.
This evidence does not close O-008 or any whole-value-movement gate and does not make the pre-existing P22 formal-cycle packet current.
The numeric reject-code mapping is a research Tau ABI convention and is not claimed to be the production canonical Python/Rust enum encoding.
